text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Kenya Human Rights Commission claims that Kenya's prisons are some of the most "cruel, inhuman and horrifying in the world."
- The National Opposition Alliance tells President Daniel arap Moi to stop interfering in the affairs of the giant milk Kenya Cooperative Creameries.
- Kenya African National Union describes as "blackmail and incitement" demands for a constitutional convention and warns that the agitators face dire consequences.
- A survey reveals that traffic police officers have formed a cartel through which they are minting thousands of shillings daily by publicly demanding bribes from motorists.

- Leading constitutional lawyer Gibson Kamau Kuria urges Attorney-General Amos Wako to prosecute four cabinet ministers who have been threatening the public with political violence in the course of their campaigns for the next general election.

- A Kenya company Mercantile Freighters Limited of Mombasa is demanding 2 million dollars damages from the government of Zanzibar for revoking a ten-year 7.5 million dollars contract to manage its rubber plantations barely one year after the pact was sealed.
- The future of Tanzania's Minister for Finance Professor Simon Mbilinyi, hangs in the balance after a parliamentary probe team finds that he has wrongly granted tax exemptions.
